findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify who builds the `unreliable` criterion->ticket-id mapping the selector consumes: state that the loop queries open tickets titled `unreliable-criterion:...`, parses the criterion id, and passes the dict to `select_candidates` (which does NOT scan tickets by title itself).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py:335 `unreliable: dict[str, str] | None = None`
fixture_selection.py:366-376 skips only when `criterion_id in unreliable` — a caller-supplied dict, not a ticket-title scan
select_from_corpus (fixture_selection.py:485-539) calls select_candidates WITHOUT any `unreliable` argument
No repo code queries open tickets by the `unreliable-criterion` title to build that mapping
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'The sibling selector already skips a criterion carrying an open ticket with that title,' but the selector does not query tickets by title. `select_candidates` skips only criteria present in a caller-supplied `unreliable: dict[str,str]` (criterion-id -> ticket-id) argument, and `select_from_corpus` does not pass `unreliable` at all. No existing code maps an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <id>` into that dict, so the breaker's 'reuse the selector' half is unimplemented as described.
findings.location: Approach / Circuit breaker: 'The sibling selector already skips a criterion carrying an open ticket with that title'
scenarios: A ticket is filed on the third failure but the next run's selector still attempts the criterion because nothing feeds the title into the `unreliable` dict

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the new logic that scans open tickets titled `unreliable-criterion:<id>` and builds the `unreliable` criterion_id->ticket_id map passed to `select_candidates`, since the selector matches on that map (not titles) and no such builder exists today.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py:335 — `select_candidates(..., unreliable: dict[str, str] | None = None, ...)` takes a precomputed criterion_id->ticket_id map, not ticket titles

findings.location: Approach -> Circuit breaker ("The sibling selector already skips a criterion carrying an open ticket with that title")
scenarios: The loop files a correctly-titled ticket but nothing feeds the selector's `unreliable` map, so the criterion is re-attempted every run and the breaker never engages

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how an open `unreliable-criterion` ticket is turned into the sibling selector's `unreliable` map at the real entry point (select_from_corpus does not currently populate it), or state that this wiring is in scope for this child.
evidence: Plan: 'The sibling selector already skips a criterion carrying an open ticket with that title, so the pair forms the breaker'
fixture_selection.py:335 `unreliable: dict[str, str] | None = None` is a parameter of select_candidates
fixture_selection.py:531-539 select_from_corpus (the real entry) calls select_candidates WITHOUT passing `unreliable`
No ticket-title→`unreliable` derivation exists in the module (search for population found only the test injection at test_fixture_selection_heldout.py:143)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the self-healing loop to file an `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` ticket for each container/ISF-class criterion the selector excludes from inline mining (reason: finder not inline-runnable), per the parent epic's explicit assignment, in addition to the three-strike breaker for residual gaps.
evidence: Parent 65dd Approach: 'the selector EXCLUDES them from inline mining and the self-healing loop files an `unreliable-criterion:` ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each; the admission runner treats a fixture whose finder rejects its shape as WITHHELD-with-reason, never a hard error.'
Parent 65dd Child decomposition: 'Coverage AC -> ... residual gaps + container/ISF criteria -> the self-healing loop, which files the `unreliable-criterion:` tickets.'

Parent 65dd Coverage AC: every routed criterion with no spec at epic-open must have 'a spec file under `.rebar/evals/`, or an open ticket titled `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` recording why it has none' — container/ISF criteria can never get a spec, so only the ticket path satisfies the AC for them.

Leaf 1cef defines failure ONLY as 'the emitted spec's candidates failed to reproduce, or ... `skipped-unbalanced`', and never mentions container/ISF, inline-runnable, or the 'finder not inline-runnable' reason.
findings.finding: The leaf's only ticket-creation trigger is the three-consecutive-failure breaker (reproduction-failure or `skipped-unbalanced`), but the parent epic explicitly assigns this same self-healing loop the duty of filing an `unreliable-criterion:` ticket for each container/ISF-class criterion (reason: finder not inline-runnable), which is a distinct trigger the leaf never covers.
findings.location: Approach → Circuit breaker (leaf 1cef); parent epic 65dd Approach ('Only inline-runnable criteria are mined') and Child decomposition ('residual gaps + container/ISF criteria -> the self-healing loop, which files the `unreliable-criterion:` tickets')
scenarios: A container criterion (e.g. G3/G4/decomp-shape) or an ISF criterion has no spec; the loop mines it, its finder rejects the inline shape (WITHHELD-with-reason), which is neither a reproduction failure nor `skipped-unbalanced`, so the breaker counter never increments and no `unreliable-criterion:` ticket is ever filed — leaving that criterion permanently in the attempt list and the parent's Coverage AC unsatisfiable for it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third disposition to the loop: when the selector/emitter reports a criterion as excluded from inline mining because its finder is container-class or ISF (not inline-runnable), file the `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` ticket immediately (reason: finder not inline-runnable) rather than routing it through the three-consecutive-failure counter, and add an acceptance criterion asserting a container/ISF criterion produces the ticket on the first run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that resolving open `unreliable-criterion:` tickets into the selector's `unreliable={criterion_id: ticket_id}` map is NEW work owned by this loop (the selector only consumes a pre-built dict and does no title scanning), rather than existing sibling behavior.
evidence: fixture_selection.py:335 `unreliable: dict[str, str] | None = None`
fixture_selection.py:368-375 skips only `if criterion_id in unreliable` — no ticket store query, no title scan
search for 'unreliable' in src/ shows the only consumer is the dict param; nothing resolves open tickets by title

But `select_candidates` (src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py:329-376) takes a pre-built `unreliable: dict[str, str]` mapping criterion-id -> ticket-id and performs NO open-ticket lookup or title matching; that resolution step is new work this loop must own, not existing reuse.
findings.location: Approach / Circuit breaker; Scope ('reuses the sibling selector')
scenarios: Implementer assumes the skip is free and omits the ticket-query/title-match code, so filed tickets never actually suppress the criterion
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase Scope/Circuit-breaker to: the loop queries open tickets, matches the `unreliable-criterion:` title, and passes `unreliable={criterion_id: ticket_id}` into the existing `select_candidates`; the selector's contribution is only the dict-keyed skip.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State where the per-criterion consecutive-failure counter is persisted, how it is keyed by criterion id, and that an admitted fixture resets it to zero.
evidence: 'The loop records, per criterion, how many consecutive runs failed to yield an admitted fixture.'
The due-stamp's storage is named ('records its last run in the repository's rebar state') but the counter's is not.
Scope lists 'the per-criterion consecutive-failure counter' as a deliverable without naming where it lives.

scenarios: An executor must decide whether the counter lives in rebar state, the ledger file, or a new file — and how it is keyed and reset on admission success.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the counter is stored in the repository's rebar state alongside the due-stamp, keyed by registry criterion id, and reset to zero whenever that criterion yields an admitted fixture.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `unreliable-criterion:` title format across creation and consumption: state whether the title uses a space, and whether it embeds the criterion id or the ticket id, matching the existing selector's `unreliable-criterion:<...>` convention (fixture_selection.py:45,373).
evidence: fixture_selection.py:45 `"unreliable-criterion:<id>"` (no space)

Reusing the existing selector requires a criterion-id->ticket-id map, so the title must be parseable back to a criterion id; the space/no-space and id-vs-ticket-id mismatch is a latent integration bug.
findings.location: Approach / Circuit breaker ('titled exactly `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>`'); AC line 2
scenarios: Loop parses open-ticket titles to rebuild the criterion->ticket map but splits on the existing no-space convention, or the title carries a criterion id where the selector reason carries a ticket id, so the round-trip fails

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the consecutive-failure counter, due-stamp, and loop ledger are updated atomically under concurrent invocations (lock/CAS/single-writer), make ticket creation idempotent (at most one ticket per criterion), and define when the counter is reset/retired (e.g. on admission, on coverage, or on ticket close).
evidence: "The loop records, per criterion, how many consecutive runs failed to yield an admitted fixture ... On the third such run it creates a ticket" — a read-modify-write with no stated atomicity
"It is also directly invocable as a command, so an operator, a cron, or any CI provider can drive it" — plus the operation-linked due-stamp — admits concurrent invocations
ABSENCE: no statement of update atomicity (lock/CAS/transaction) for the counter/stamp/ledger, and no RETIRE/reset path for the counter once a criterion is covered or its ticket closed
findings.finding: The plan introduces three pieces of persisted shared state — the due-stamp, the per-criterion consecutive-failure counter, and the loop's own ledger file — but does not specify concurrency/ownership of updates nor a retirement path for the counter. The counter update is a check-then-act (read count, increment, and at 3 create a ticket), and the plan explicitly allows multiple triggers (operator, cron, any CI provider, and the operation-linked due-stamp) to drive the loop. Two overlapping runs could both read the same count, double-increment, or double-create the `unreliable-criterion:` ticket, and the counter has no stated reset when a criterion becomes covered or its ticket is closed.
findings.location: Approach → Circuit breaker / Portability; Scope ("the per-criterion consecutive-failure counter", "the loop's own ledger file")
scenarios: Two runs fire near-simultaneously (operator run overlapping the due-stamp-triggered operation run): both increment the same counter or both create the ticket, yielding a duplicate ticket or a miscounted breaker
A criterion is covered by a fixture; its stale counter persists, and if a fixture is later removed the breaker is already partway tripped from history that no longer applies
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Concurrency & state lifecycle' note: serialize a run via a repository lock (single writer), make the counter increment and ticket creation idempotent (create the ticket only if none with that exact title is open), and reset a criterion's counter to zero when it is admitted or when its `unreliable-criterion:` ticket is closed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify per-run observability: a log/record of criteria attempted, admitted, failed (with failure kind), tickets filed, and the budget-stop, surfaced not swallowed.
evidence: Absence: no section mentions logging, metrics, or operator-visible output for run outcomes, failures, or breaker trips.
'while the ticket is open the criterion costs nothing' — an unattended loop with no run log leaves operators blind to why a criterion stopped being attempted.
findings.finding: The loop adds new failure points (LLM admission calls, ledger file I/O, ticket writes, counter writes) but plans no observability — no metric/log/trace for runs, per-criterion failures, tickets created, or budget stops.
scenarios: An unattended 30-day loop stops attempting a criterion; an operator has no log/metric explaining whether it was budget, unbalanced, or the breaker.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a structured run record (or log lines) enumerating attempted/admitted/failed criteria, failure kind per criterion, tickets created, and the headroom-stop decision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the write ordering / idempotency for counter-increment vs ticket-creation and how a crash mid-run reconciles the ledger reservation.
evidence: 'On the third such run it creates a ticket' — counter update and ticket creation are two writes with no stated atomicity or ordering guarantee.
'the run stops with completed criteria admitted and their spend reconciled' — reconciliation on crash (vs clean BudgetExceeded) is not covered.
findings.finding: Partial-state durability is not addressed: if a run crashes between incrementing a criterion's counter and creating the ticket (or between reserving budget and reconciling spend), the resulting state may double-count or lose a failure.
scenarios: Process is killed mid-run after a counter increment but before the ticket write; next run re-increments or files late.
Crash after ledger reserve but before admission reconcile leaves reserved-but-unspent headroom.
findings.suggested_fix: Make ticket creation idempotent on the exact title (selector already skips it) and increment the counter after admission resolves; document that an unreconciled reservation is released or recovered on the next run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the breaker threshold and per-run cap configurable (like the interval) with stated defaults, and capture the loop/breaker/due-stamp design in an ADR or AGENTS.md.
evidence: 'On the third such run it creates a ticket' — the threshold 3 is a fixed literal.
'ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=25.0)' — the cap is a literal.
Only the interval is described as 'configured'; the breaker threshold and cap are not.
Absence: no ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc update is listed for the new loop/breaker pattern.
findings.finding: Two evolving thresholds — the '3 consecutive failures' breaker trip and the '$25' cap — are hardcoded (cap_usd=25.0 appears as a literal), and no ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc capture is planned for this novel self-healing-loop + circuit-breaker + due-stamp pattern.
findings.location: Approach / Circuit breaker, Unattended spend bound; Non-goals
scenarios: Tuning the breaker sensitivity or per-interval spend later requires a code edit rather than config.
A future maintainer meets the due-stamp/breaker pattern with no design record.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose max-consecutive-failures and cap_usd as configuration defaulting to 3 and 25.0, and add an ADR describing the gap-only convergence, circuit breaker, and operation-linked due-stamp.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Situate the 'circuit breaker' against the canonical consecutive-failure breaker (note the deliberate absence of automatic half-open/timeout reset — re-entry is manual ticket closure) and disambiguate from the existing in-repo reconciler 'circuit breaker' (ADR 0027/0028, _config_schema), or rename to a quarantine/trip-and-file term.
evidence: Plan: 'The loop records, per criterion, how many consecutive runs failed ... On the third such run it creates a ticket titled exactly `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` ... and stops attempting that criterion.'

External prior art (retrieved, microservices.io/patterns/reliability/circuit-breaker.html): 'When the number of consecutive failures crosses a threshold, the circuit breaker trips, and for the duration of a timeout period all attempts ... fail immediately' — rebar's variant has no automatic half-open/timeout; re-entry requires a human closing a ticket, so it is a quarantine, not a classic breaker.
In-repo prior art: docs/adr/0028-... and 0027-... 'circuit breaker (refuse a pass mutating/retiring > N% of bindings)'; src/rebar/_config_schema.py:535 'Convergence circuit breaker (epic 3006-e198)'.
findings.finding: The plan labels its mechanism a 'circuit breaker' but neither situates it against the canonical external circuit-breaker pattern nor against the existing in-repo circuit breaker (ADR 0027/0028 reconciler breaker; the 'Convergence circuit breaker' in _config_schema); the mechanism is actually a persistent ticket-based quarantine, and the naming/lack-of-comparison risks confusion and reinvention.
scenarios: A reader expects classic breaker semantics (automatic half-open probe / timeout-based reset) that this design deliberately does not provide, since re-entry is manual ticket closure.
The term collides with the reconciler's established 'circuit breaker' concept, muddying which mechanism is meant.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the transient-retry with a stated max-attempts/backoff and add an acceptance criterion exercising retry and the 'ceiling wins over transient failure' precedence.
evidence: 'A transient model or transport error inside a criterion's admission attempt is RETRYABLE and retried within the run.'
No AC covers retry behavior or the 'when a transient failure and the ceiling coincide, the ceiling wins' rule.
No retry count, attempt limit, or backoff is stated, so retries are unbounded as written.
findings.finding: The RETRYABLE transient-error path is described but bounded by no stated retry count/backoff and is exercised by no acceptance criterion.
scenarios: A criterion that transiently fails repeatedly within a run could retry indefinitely, defeating the per-interval spend bound.
The 'ceiling wins' precedence rule ships unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: State a max retry count with backoff per criterion, and add an AC asserting that a stubbed runner raising a transient error then succeeding admits within the attempt bound, and that a coincident BudgetExceeded stops the run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the $25 pre-flight is the existing `run_admission` `cap_usd`/`reserve_usd` reserve threaded through (not a second, loop-level budget gate), citing fixture_admission.py:173-178.
evidence: fixture_admission.py:69-85 `run_admission(..., cap_usd, reserve_usd, ...)`
fixture_admission.py:173-178 already reserves per criterion via `ledger.reserve(...)`
ledger.py:86-111 `reserve(..., cap_usd, reserve_usd)` is the single existing choke point
findings.finding: The plan describes a per-run pre-flight 'through `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=25.0)`' as the loop's own stop condition, but `run_admission` (src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:173-178) already calls `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=..., reserve_usd=...)` per criterion internally and stops on `BudgetExceeded`. The plan should clarify it is threading its $25 cap through the existing runner's reserve, not adding a second parallel budgeting layer, to avoid duplicate/competing spend gates.
findings.location: Approach / Unattended spend bound; Scope ('reuses ... admission runner')
scenarios: Implementer builds a separate loop-level reserve loop in addition to the runner's, producing two budget accountings that can disagree
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the spend-bound section to: the loop invokes `run_admission(..., cap_usd=25.0, ledger_path=<loop ledger>)`, relying on the runner's built-in per-criterion `ledger.reserve` to stop on `BudgetExceeded`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the ticket-title format with the existing `unreliable-criterion:<id>` (no-space) convention in fixture_selection.py:373 — state whether the loop's title parser tolerates both, or align the mandated title to the existing form.

scenarios: The loop files a title with a space; a title-parser modeled on the existing no-space `unreliable-criterion:<id>` reason string fails to match, so the criterion is re-attempted

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the mandated title prefix `unreliable-criterion: ` (with space) against the codebase's existing no-space convention `unreliable-criterion:<id>` (fixture_selection.py:45,373) and state which form both the creator and the title->map parser use.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the exact `unreliable-criterion` title string (space vs no space) and the identifier used (registry criterion id vs ticket id) with the sibling selector's existing convention in fixture_selection.py before locking it into the ACs.
evidence: Plan: 'titled exactly `unreliable-criterion: <criterion-id>` — the literal prefix `unreliable-criterion: ` followed by the registry criterion id'
fixture_selection.py:45 documents the reason string as `unreliable-criterion:<id>` (no space)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the due-stamp trigger against the existing operation-linked trigger family (rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger / compact_trigger and their shared stamped-lock helper in _proc.py) and ADR 0005/0106: state whether this loop reuses that machinery or justify a distinct mechanism, and cite ADR 0106's identical portability argument and 30-day default rather than re-deriving them.
evidence: Plan: 'The trigger is operation-linked with an in-process due-stamp: the loop records its last run in the repository's rebar state, and a rebar plan-review operation ... advances it when the configured interval has elapsed, defaulting to 30 days. It is also directly invocable as a command...'

ADR 0005 (docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:138-145): 'The cadence floor is now an operation-linked trigger (rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger, mirroring the compaction trigger...): the tail of an attested gate resolution performs one O(1) stat of a <root>/gc/last-pass.stamp sidecar against the janitor interval_seconds, and when due spawns a detached child...'

ADR 0106 (docs/adr/0106-...:52-55): 'a plain duration in config, with no dependency on any single CI provider ... an operator with no CI can run it by hand or by cron, exactly as compact-all already degrades' and default 30 days (line 48).
src/rebar/_proc.py:19: the detached-spawn/trigger pattern 'was previously copied per site' — a deliberate de-duplication the plan's fourth copy would regress.
Shared stamped-lock helper exercised across both triggers: tests/unit/store/test_stamped_lock.py referencing _commands/compact_trigger.py and _snapshot/gc_trigger.py.
findings.finding: The 'operation-linked due-stamp' trigger reinvents an existing, named, de-duplicated in-repo pattern (rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger / rebar._commands.compact_trigger sharing a stamped-lock helper) without acknowledging or reusing it, and re-argues portability from scratch though ADR 0106 already made the same argument and set the same 30-day default.
scenarios: Reviewer/implementer builds a new bespoke stamp+interval+single-flight mechanism instead of extending gc_trigger's shared machinery, duplicating the stamped-lock/detached-spawn logic and its concurrency guarantees.
The plan's portability rationale is treated as novel reasoning when it is a re-derivation of an accepted ADR.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Portability naming rebar._snapshot.gc_trigger as the prior art the due-stamp mirrors, commit to reusing the shared stamped-lock/detached-spawn helper (_proc.py) for single-flight, and reference ADR 0106 for the config-driven-interval / no-CI-dependency / 30-day-default rationale instead of restating it.

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)
